description:
TYPE: line chart

TITLE: Nominal versus Real Minimum Wage

TEXT IN IMAGE: 
- Title: Nominal versus Real Minimum Wage
- Y-axis labels: $0.00, $2.00, $4.00, $6.00, $8.00, $10.00, $12.00
- X-axis labels: 1940, 1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010
- Legend: 
  - (Orange line) Nominal Minimum Wage
  - (Blue line) Real Minimum Wage
- Sources: U.S. Department of Labor. History of Federal Minimum Wage Rates under the Fair Labor Standards Act, 1938–2009. (Some data from CPI Inflation Calculator, https://data.bls.gov/cgi-bin/cpicalc.pl.)

DATA: 
- Axes: X-axis represents years from 1940 to 2010; Y-axis represents dollar amount from $0.00 to $12.00.
- Series 1: Nominal Minimum Wage (orange line showing step-wise increases over time, starting around $0.25 in 1940 and rising to just over $7.00 by 2010).
- Series 2: Real Minimum Wage (blue fluctuating line showing purchasing power, peaking near $11.5ond around 1968, and generally trending differently than the nominal wage).

KEY FACTS:
- The graph compares the Nominal Minimum Wage and the Real Minimum Wage from 1940 to around 2015.
- The Nominal Minimum Wage shows a consistent step-wise upward trend over the decades.
- The Real Minimum Wage (purchasing power) fluctuates significantly, reaching its peak around 1968 at approximately $11.50.
- In later years, the real minimum wage drops significantly below its historical peak, while the nominal minimum wage reaches its highest point shown around 2010.
